Between:
The United India Insurance Company Limited,
Rep. by its Branch Manager,
H.No.80-121/6A, Ashok Nagar,
Miryalguda Town, Nalgonda District.

.....Appellant
 And
Sorupu Savithramma
and three others.

....Respondents
 Judgment
This appeal is filed by the appellant/Insurance Company challenging the award and decree dated
28.12.2018 passed in O.P.No.302 of 2014 by the Chairman, Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal-cum-I
Additional

District Judge at Nalgonda (for short "the Tribunal"), wherein the Tribunal granted a total compensation of Rs.5,11,800/- with interest @ 7.5% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realization against the claim of Rs.9,00,000/- for the death of Sorupu Ramulu (hereinafter referred as "the deceased").
2.
Heard the submissions of learned counsel for both sides and perused the record.

3. The learned Standing Counsel for the appellant/Insurance Company contended that the Tribunal erred in fastening liability on the insurer as the driver of the crime vehicle did not possess a valid and effective driving license at the time of the accident.
It is further contended that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is excessive.

4. On the other hand, the learned counsel for the respondent Nos.1 and 2/claimants contended that the accident occurred solely due to the rash and negligent driving of the rider of the Motor Cycle bearing No.AP-24-AB-4596.

It is further contended that the deceased was a centering mastry earning Rs.15,000/- per month and the family has lost its sole breadwinner, leaving them destitute and therefore, prayed this Court to enhance the compensation.
It is asserted that the insurer is liable to indemnify the owner as the policy was in force as on the date of the accident.

sentences.text: As seen from the material placed on record, the accident occurred on 04.10.2013 when the crime vehicle dashed the deceased's motorcycle near the Market office of Nidmanoor.
The police registered a case in Cr.No.121 of 2013 for the offences under Sections 304-A and 337 of IPC.
Based on the evidence of PW.1 and PW.2 (eye-witness), and Ex.A1 to A6, the Tribunal rightly concluded that the accident was a result of the rash and negligent driving of the crime vehicle's driver.
6. Sofaras as compensation is concerned, the Tribunal fixed the notional income at Rs.3,000/- per month as no documentary evidence of earnings was produced.

Considering the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Shaikh Sadik Shaikh Rafique v. Reliance General Insurance Company Ltd. &
others1, this Court deems it appropriate to take the notional income at Rs.6,000/- per month.

sentences.text: Taking the monthly income as Rs.6,000/-, the annual income is arrived at Rs.72,000/-.

Adding 25%
towards future prospects for the deceased aged 43 years, the total annual income is Rs.90,000/-.
After deducting 1/3rd (Rs.30,000/-) towards personal and living expenses for two dependent family members, the annual contribution to the family comes to Rs.60,000/-.
Applying the multiplier of 14 for the relevant age group, the total loss of dependency is calculated at Rs.8,40,000/-.

Further, as per the principles laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Pranay Sethi 2, the appellants-claimants are also entitled to Rs.91,000/- (Rs.70,000/- + 10% enhancement 2025 INSC 673 2(2017) 16 SCC 680 for every three years) under the conventional heads.

sentences.text:
Accordingly, the total compensation comes to Rs.9,31,000/-.
7.
At this stage, learned Standing Counsel for the Insurance Company contends that the claimants had sought only Rs.9,00,000/- and therefore compensation cannot exceed the amount claimed.

However, in view of the judgments of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Laxman @ Laxman Mourya Vs.
Divisional Manager, Oriental Insurance Company Limited and another 3and Nagappa Vs.
Gurudayal Singh 4, and considering that the Motor Vehicles Act is a beneficial legislation intended to ensure just and fair compensation, the Courts are empowered to award compensation in excess of the amount claimed.

entities.text:
Laxman @ Laxman Mourya Vs.
Divisional Manager, Oriental Insurance Company Limited and another 3and Nagappa Vs.
Gurudayal Singh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, the claimants are entitled to the higher amount now assessed.

8. In the result, this appeal is disposed of and the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is enhanced from Rs.5,11,800/- to Rs.9,31,000/- with interest @ 7.5% per annum from the date of claim petition till the date of realization.
The respondent Nos.1 and 2 shall pay deficit Court fee on the enhanced compensation amount.

The appellant/Insurance Company is directed to deposit the compensation amount with interest within a (2011) 10 SCC 756 2003 ACJ 12 (SC) period of two (02)
months from the date of receipt of copy of this judgment.
On such deposit, the claimants are permitted to withdraw the same.
No order as to costs.
As a sequel, the miscellaneous petitions pending, if any, shall stand closed.
